We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, one with a methyl para to sulfonamide, the other phenyl attached to a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamamide) with an aniline (para amino) on that phenyl? Actually Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an amino at para? Wait Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with two amino groups? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the amide nitrogen attaches to phenyl which has an amino substituent at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amino at position 1 (attached to N) and another amino at position? Actually "c3ccccc3" is phenyl, preceded by N (amide N) attached to carbonyl, then "c3ccccc3N" means the phenyl has an N attached at the end (aniline). So it's a phenyl with an amino substituent (aniline). So overall target is a sulfonamide linking a tolyl (methyl phenyl) to a phenyl bearing a trans-cinnamamide with an aniline para? Actually the phenyl attached to sulfonyl has a para substituent of the cinnamamide chain.

Thus retrosynthesis: disconnection 1: sulfonamide formation between tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl aryl (p-phenyl with cinnamamide). So step 1: combine p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) with aryl sulfonyl chloride (p-(cinnamoylamino)phenylsulfonyl chloride). That sulfonyl chloride can be made from the corresponding sulfonic acid (aryl sulfonic acid) via chlorination (SO2Cl). The aryl sulfonic acid can be made from sulfonation of the phenyl ring (electrophilic aromatic substitution) of the phenyl bearing the cinnamamide chain.

Thus route: target -> disconnection at S-N bond (sulfonamide). Precursors: 4-methylaniline (commercial) and 4-(cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid). Next disconnection: the sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonation of 4-(cinnamoylamino)benzene (i.e., 4-(cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonic acid). So step 2: sulfonation of 4-(cinnamoylamino)benzene using chlorosulfonic acid (ClSO3H) to give sulfonyl chloride directly (or sulfonic acid then convert). So precursor: 4-(cinnamoylamino)benzene (commercial? maybe not). Could be made via amide coupling of 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Actually the cinnamoylamide: we need to attach C=O-NH-Ph-NH2? Wait the chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So we need an aniline (para-aminophenyl) to be amidated with trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative). So step 3: amide formation between trans-cinnamic acid (or its acid chloride) and p-phenylenediamine? Actually we need an aniline with an amino group at para to the amide. The phenyl ring has an amide at position 1 (attached to carbonyl) and an amino at position 4. So we could start from p-phenylenediamine (commercial) and selectively acylate one amino with trans-cinnamoyl chloride (or activated acid). That yields the desired 4-(cinnamoylamino)aniline (i.e., 4-aminobenzamide). Then sulfonate that aromatic ring at para to the amide (which is the other para position? Actually the amide is at position 1, the amino at position 4. Sulfonation would occur at the other para? Wait the sulfonyl group attaches to the phenyl ring at position 4 relative to amide? In target, the sulfonyl attaches to phenyl at para to the amide (i.e., the phenyl attached to sulfonyl has the cinnamamide at para). So the phenyl ring that gets sulfonated is the same as the one bearing the cinnamamide. So we need to sulfonate the phenyl ring at the position para to the amide (which is also the position of the sulfonyl group). Starting from 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine) after mono-acylation, we have an aniline at para to amide. That aniline can be sulfonated to give sulfonyl chloride at that position (para to amide). However sulfonation of an aniline may be problematic due to activation; but we can protect the amino (e.g., as acetamide) then sulfonate, then deprotect. But we have only 3 steps total, so we need minimal steps. Maybe we can reverse: first sulfonate p-phenylenediamine to give sulfonyl chloride at one amino, then protect the other, then amide formation. But we need final product with both sulfonamide and amide. The sulfonyl chloride will react with p-toluidine later.

Simplify: Use commercially available 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride) and then amidate the aniline? But we need sulfonyl attached to phenyl that also has amide substituent. Could we start from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride and perform amide coupling at the para amino? That would give sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl with amide at para. Then react with p-toluidine to form sulfonamide. However the sulfonyl chloride is needed for sulfonamide formation; but after amide coupling, the sulfonyl chloride remains (since we used the aniline). So step 1: start with 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). Step 2: amidate the amino with trans-cinnamoyl chloride to give 4-(cinnamoylamido)benzenesulfonyl chloride. Step 3: react with p-toluidine to give final sulfonamide. That's 3 steps, all using commercially available reagents. Need to check availability and price under $9999.

We need to verify that 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride is commercially available. Likely yes (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride). Also trans-cinnamoyl chloride is commercially available. p-toluidine is commercial.

Thus route:

Target (SMILES) -> retrosynthesis step: disconnection of sulfonamide S-N bond -> precursors: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and 4-(cinnamoylamido)benzenesulfonyl chloride.

Second disconnection: disconnection of amide bond between cinnamoyl and aniline -> precursors: trans-cinnamoyl chloride and p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride.

Thus final leaves: p-toluidine, trans-cinnamoyl chloride, p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride. All commercially available.

Now we need to provide JSON with reaction nodes and template IDs. We need template IDs for sulfonamide formation (reaction of sulfonyl chloride with amine) and amide formation (acyl chloride with amine). We need to find appropriate template IDs via search.

Search for sulfonamide formation: molecule_smiles of product maybe "c1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1" (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride). Let's search for template that forms sulfonamide from sulfonyl chloride and amine.
